newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgacom sees 1996 sales up nine percent, higher profit.
newsitem.headline: Belgacom sees 1996 sales up nine percent, higher profit.

text.p: Belgian state telephone company Belgacom said on Thursday its provisional consolidated turnover rose 9.4 percent to 139 billion francs ($4 billion) in 1996.
It said in a statement it also expected 1996 full-year consolidated net profit rose in line with the rise in the first half of the year.
Belgacom had a 1996 first-half group net profit of 6.6 billion francs, up 15.0 percent from a year earlier.

It said in the statement the driving force behind the increase of turnover was its Belgacom Mobile subsidiary, which operates Belgium's first GSM network and the old analogue mobile phone network. Belgacom Mobile is 25 percent owned by U.S. AirTouch Communications.
Belgacom Mobile had 410,172 clients by the end of 1996, against 235,238 a year earlier.
Total group investments have been scaled down to 28 billion francs, against 44 billion in 1995.
Group financial debt remained steady at 90 billion francs despite the payment of nine billion francs to the government for the mobile phone licence in 1996.
Belgacom said that its pension fund, which was created in July 1995, had 63 billion francs on December 31, 1996, compared with 46 billion a year earlier.
Belgacom said a general shareholders meeting has been scheduled for April 30. Full earnings will be published after approval of the annual accounts by the board, which is due to meet on February 20.

Belgacom is 49.9 percent owned by a consortium comprising Ameritech, Singapore Telecom, TeleDanmark and three Belgian investors. The remaining shares are held by the Belgian state. ($1=33.78 Belgian Franc)
